target.scope: RungProof non-catalog LAD editor controls and project-tree object commands
target.claimBoundary: This registry records implementation locations, required checks, and evidence gaps. It does not promote broad command logs to per-gate passes, prove an installed-TIA match, prove project import/export compatibility, or establish live-PLC behavior.

localStatus.not-assessed: No exact structured artifact records this stable gate ID and all required assertions.
localStatus.automated-pass: An exact structured artifact records this gate ID, every required assertion, and a passing result.
localStatus.automated-fail: An exact structured artifact records this gate ID and at least one failed required assertion.

vendorStatus.not-assessed: No exact official source or matched installed-TIA evidence is bound to this gate.
vendorStatus.source-only: An official Siemens source describes the behavior, but no same-state installed-TIA comparison is bound.
vendorStatus.matched: A same-state installed-TIA comparison is bound with immutable identity and review metadata.

implementationStatus.present: The bounded behavior is implemented in the current source tree.
implementationStatus.bounded-subset: A deliberately narrower behavior is implemented and the excluded behavior is explicit.

evidencePolicy.qualifyingLocalEvidence: A JSON result emitted by the production command path with one result object per gate. Each object must contain the exact gateId, status, required assertion outcomes, command identity, source/build identity, timestamps, and the fixed externalTia=false and livePlc=false boundaries.
nonQualifyingEvidence: A broad process exit code or PASS line without a per-gate JSON result.
A runner command whose gateIds array is empty.
A unit-test or native-verifier log that combines unrelated controls without an exact gate record.
Source presence, documentation prose, or an unreviewed screenshot by itself.
evidencePolicy.currentAssessment: Exact structured production-path artifacts pass all 17 local gates (105 assertions). These artifacts remain offline-only and do not establish installed-TIA, import/export, or live-PLC parity.

structuredSweepContracts.runnerExpectation: Add this command to the interaction and full profiles in tools/Invoke-TiaParitySuite.ps1 only after it writes and validates the declared artifact. The runner command must attach exactly these seven gateIds.
structuredSweepContracts.resultExpectation: The artifact must contain exactly seven unique gate results, reject missing or extra IDs, and fail the process if any required assertion is absent or false.

structuredSweepContracts.runnerExpectation: Add this command to the interaction and full profiles in tools/Invoke-TiaParitySuite.ps1 only after it writes and validates the declared artifact. The runner command must attach exactly these ten gateIds.
structuredSweepContracts.resultExpectation: The artifact must contain exactly ten unique gate results, reject missing or extra IDs, and fail the process if any required assertion is absent or false.

gates.title: Focused LAD F9/F10 contact shortcuts
gates.behavior: With the visible LAD canvas focused, unmodified F9 inserts a normally open contact and unmodified F10 inserts a normally closed contact at the selected insertion point. Unfocused, hidden, and modifier-bearing input must not masquerade as these shortcuts; Undo must restore the prior document.
requiredAssertions: visible focused LAD accepts unmodified F9 as NO insertion
visible focused LAD accepts unmodified F10 as NC insertion
unfocused and hidden LAD reject the shortcuts
modifier-bearing F9/F10 retain their separate meanings
each insertion is one undoable edit and Undo restores the exact baseline
limitations: The exact local gate artifact is automated and offline; it is not a same-state installed-TIA keyboard comparison.
No same-state installed-TIA keyboard comparison is bound.

gates.title: Operand-entry and edit shortcuts
gates.behavior: Return or typing opens the first operand, F2 edits the selected operand, Enter applies, Escape discards, Ctrl+I opens suggestions, and Ctrl+Shift+I exposes RungProof's create-and-assign action. Pointer routing must resolve the exact rendered pin or property form.
requiredAssertions: Return opens an empty first-operand editor
typing opens the first-operand editor with the typed character
F2 opens the selected operand
Enter applies exactly once and Escape leaves document and history unchanged
Ctrl+I opens suggestions and Ctrl+Shift+I exposes create-and-assign
viewport pointer routing selects the exact pin or instruction property form
limitations: RungProof create-and-assign is not claimed to be TIA's exact define-tag dialog.
The current broad transaction and placement logs are not per-gate structured evidence.

gates.title: Pending editor transaction resolution
gates.behavior: Navigation, document changes, and project actions must not silently lose staged editor state. Apply continues only after a successful commit; discard continues without mutation; cancel preserves the current document, history, selection, and destination.
requiredAssertions: failed Apply does not run the queued continuation
successful Apply commits one edit then runs the continuation once
Discard runs the continuation without applying the draft
Cancel runs no continuation and preserves document and history
multiple pending forms resolve deterministically without partial commit
limitations: This is a RungProof integrity gate, not an assertion that TIA uses the same dialog or transaction architecture.

gates.title: Editor command target and history integrity
gates.behavior: Context, toolbar, menu, and keyboard commands must act on the exact current target, reject stale popup targets, preserve unrelated network conditions, and produce one bounded Undo/Redo transaction.
requiredAssertions: context commands preserve the selected slot or element identity
stale popup targets are rejected without document mutation
output copy, paste, and delete preserve unrelated conditions
toolbar, context, and keyboard routes converge on the same bounded mutation
Undo and Redo restore exact serialized states
limitations: The structured gate artifact binds the command routes and exact serialized Undo/Redo assertions, but it does not establish vendor UI equivalence.

gates.title: Operand and tag-information view controls
gates.behavior: Symbolic, Absolute, and Both operand representation must remain independent from Hidden, Show, and Hierarchical tag information and from On operands versus Below network positioning. Hidden must remove supplementary information without removing the operand or changing literals and missing-value markers.
requiredAssertions: all 18 representation by information by position combinations execute
numeric literals and ??? remain operands in every combination
Hidden yields no supplementary on-operand or below-network information
Show and Hierarchical place information at exactly one selected location
structured leaf and parent comments follow the bounded hierarchy rule
limitations: The local model covers one bounded structured-comment hierarchy and does not prove all TIA operand classes.
The exact local gate artifact binds the 18-case result; the remaining boundary is an installed-TIA comparison across the same combinations.

gates.title: Per-block selection, scroll, and zoom state
gates.behavior: Each program block retains its own stable selection target, scroll offsets, and zoom across navigation. Pending edits block navigation, and a deleted saved target falls back safely to the network header rather than restoring a stale selection.
requiredAssertions: block A restores its exact stable target, scroll, and zoom
block B restores its exact stable target, scroll, and zoom
pending Apply failure or Cancel prevents navigation and state storage
a deleted saved target falls back to the header and zero scroll
the restored scrolled viewport still renders instructions
limitations: The current verifier is scripted and explicitly reports physicalInput=false.
No installed-TIA view-state comparison is bound.

gates.title: Empty LAD instruction placeholder and chooser
gates.behavior: The unresolved ??? box is an editor-only placeholder with continuous input lead and a chooser limited to the supported terminal-box operations. Every choice must replace the placeholder with the exact operation and survive JSON save/reload; the unresolved placeholder is never executable.
requiredAssertions: the unresolved placeholder opens its chooser through the production route
the chooser contains exactly the declared supported choices
each choice creates the exact expected terminal operation
replacement clears the placeholder and persists through save/reload
the unresolved placeholder cannot compile or execute as an instruction
limitations: The chooser is intentionally limited to RungProof-supported boxes and is not a Siemens catalog-completeness claim.
The existing verifier returns one broad boolean and emits no exact gate artifact.

gates.title: Project-tree selection versus activation
gates.behavior: Single-click selects without opening. Double-click or focused Enter activates supported program-block, tag-table, watch-table, Global DB, generated instance DB, and creation-command rows through the production ItemActivated route.
requiredAssertions: single-click selects every supported row without opening it
double-click activates every supported object and command row
focused Enter activates the selected supported row
activation opens the exact matching document or dialog
returning from an instance DB restores the correct active block title
limitations: Current pointer output aggregates all object and command routes into one broad result string.

gates.title: Show all tags navigation row
gates.behavior: The Show all tags row is a navigation object: selection does not open it, activation opens the central tag document without filtering to one named table, and navigation alone does not dirty project content.
requiredAssertions: the Show all tags row is present with stable metadata
selection alone leaves the current document open
activation opens the unfiltered tag document with the matching title
all tag tables are represented without changing active project content
navigation does not change the serialized content baseline
limitations: The dedicated structured project-tree artifact isolates this row locally; no installed-TIA navigation comparison is bound.

gates.title: Add new block command
gates.behavior: Activation opens the create-block dialog. The bounded choices are OB, FB, FC, and supported Global DB; blank or duplicate names are rejected atomically, valid creation persists, the tree row appears, and Undo/Redo restores exact states.
requiredAssertions: selection does not open the dialog and activation does
OB, FB, FC, and Global DB choices are explicit
blank and duplicate names are rejected without history mutation
valid creation persists and creates the exact tree row
Undo, Redo, and cleanup reproduce exact serialized states
limitations: ARRAY DB, type-based DB, manual instance DB, software-unit release, and add-and-open variants are unsupported.

gates.title: Add new tag table command
gates.behavior: Activation opens the named tag-table dialog. Blank and duplicate names are rejected atomically; valid creation persists, creates the exact tree row, and participates in Undo/Redo.
requiredAssertions: selection does not open the dialog and activation does
blank and duplicate names are rejected without history mutation
valid creation persists with stable name and exact tree row
Undo removes and Redo restores the exact table
active-table navigation does not itself dirty project content
limitations: Tag-table rename and tag-table delete are not implemented and are listed as unsupported below.

gates.title: Add new watch table command
gates.behavior: Activation opens the named watch-table dialog. Blank and case-insensitive duplicate names are rejected atomically; valid creation persists independently, creates the exact tree row, and participates in Undo/Redo.
requiredAssertions: selection does not open the dialog and activation does
blank and case-insensitive duplicate names are rejected without history mutation
valid creation persists with independent symbols and exact tree row
Undo removes and Redo restores the exact table
selecting another table is navigation rather than a content edit
limitations: Watch-table rename is not implemented and is listed as unsupported below.

gates.title: Supported Global DB object contract
gates.behavior: A supported optimized-access Global DB appears under Program blocks and activates a declaration document with scalar Name, Data type, Start value, Retain, and Comment fields. DB member actions use member-specific labels and DB defaults, including on initial DB entry and after switching between DB and FB documents. The DB screen exposes an Edit members action that opens the Project objects member form at a usable dock width and a Project tree return action. Existing declarations can be selected and transactionally edited; starting a new member resolves any pending form through Apply, Discard, or Cancel. Selection is scoped to its owning block and persistent member ID, with a legacy name/index fallback only for declarations without IDs. It has no LAD networks and cannot be a CALL, task, or program-entry target.
requiredAssertions: the Global DB row appears under Program blocks
activation opens declarations and not a LAD canvas
Name, Data type, Start value, Retain, and Comment persist
starting a new member resolves the pending form without silently discarding or mutating it
changing a new member type seeds a valid initial value, including an ENUM value that belongs to its member domain
editing an ENUM domain reseeds untouched initial values; valid domains apply and invalid domains are rejected atomically
a Retain-only edit is pending, cancelable, and resolved before navigation
initial DB entry and DB-to-FB-to-DB navigation refresh member labels and defaults
the DB action opens the visible member form at widened dock width and returns to the tree at the exact prior dock width
a selected declaration remains selected by persistent member ID after same-DB row insertion and edits the same member
declaration selection is cleared when activation changes the owning block
switching blocks leaves the other DB declaration byte-identical
LAD network insertion is rejected
CALL, task, and program-entry target selection excludes the DB
limitations: Only the documented scalar optimized-access subset is supported.
Standard-access DB-wide retention, other columns, access modes, compound DB types, and runtime DB-member addressing are not implemented.

gates.title: Generated instance DB object contract
gates.behavior: Generated FB, timer, and counter instance DB identities appear under Program blocks, activate a read-only definition document, display inherited FB defaults as effective start values, preserve unique DB number/name identity, and return cleanly to the owning block without a stale title.
requiredAssertions: the generated instance DB row appears under Program blocks
selection does not open and activation opens the exact definition
DB number and symbolic name are unique and persist
the read-only instance table renders inherited defaults as start values for FB Input, Output, Static and IEC timer/counter members, excludes TEMP locals, and discloses unsupported overrides
returning to the owner restores the correct block title and canvas
limitations: Per-instance start-value overrides, online monitor values, offsets, and extended DB attributes are not modeled.
Manual instance DB creation, multi-instance storage, and parameter-instance storage are unsupported.

gates.title: Program-block drag to LAD CALL target
gates.behavior: Dragging a supported FC or FB row to a visible terminal target resolves the production tree payload, validates the canvas drop, and opens CALL authoring. Cancel must be exact and history-free; Apply must create the exact target call as one undoable edit with exact Undo/Redo.
requiredAssertions: only supported program-block rows produce a CALL drag payload
the visible terminal accepts the exact payload and rejects invalid targets
drop opens CALL authoring for the exact source block
Cancel preserves exact serialized state and creates no Undo entry
Apply, Undo, and Redo reproduce exact serialized states
limitations: The current Windows verifier calls the production payload and canvas drop methods at measured visible coordinates because headless native drag-threshold synthesis is unreliable.
Multi-instance and parameter-instance FB calls remain unsupported.

gates.title: Active-workspace watch-table deletion
gates.behavior: Deletion is supported only for the active watch table through the watch-table workspace button. It removes exactly that table as one project metadata edit, supports Undo/Redo, selects a surviving table, and refuses to delete the final table.
requiredAssertions: the workspace delete button targets only the active watch table
deletion removes exactly one table and preserves all survivors
Undo and Redo restore exact serialized states and active selection
the delete control is disabled or rejected when one table remains
no project-tree row context-delete route is exposed
limitations: This gate does not claim project-tree row deletion; that route is explicitly unsupported.
Watch-table rename is unsupported.

gates.title: Remove selected watch-table symbol
gates.behavior: The workspace Remove button removes the selected symbol from the active watch table. Other symbols and other watch tables remain unchanged; the mutation participates in Undo/Redo and project Save/Load.
requiredAssertions: Remove deletes the selected symbol from the active table, preserves other symbols and tables, and refreshes the visible count
Undo and Redo restore exact watch-table JSON and active selection
Save/Load retains the removed symbol's absence in the active table and its presence in another table
limitations: Address-based watch entries, display-format editing, online monitor values, and physical PLC modification are outside this gate.

unsupportedDocumented.boundary: Named tag tables can be created, selected, opened, and persisted, but no rename command or model operation exists.
Tag tables are not deletable. This avoids silently orphaning or reassigning contained tag declarations until an explicit migration contract exists.
Named watch tables can be created, selected, opened, persisted, and deleted through the active workspace, but no rename command or model operation exists.
The project-tree row exposes selection and activation only. Watch-table deletion is available only from the active watch-table workspace, and the final remaining table is protected.
